title: TestAForceAddedReportIsCaughtAtCollect is flaky under the full parallel run
description:
The artifact-boundary backstop test fails intermittently in a whole-suite run and passes every time in isolation.

Observed 2026-09-13 on the wave-6 integration tree:
- Full 'go test -short ./...': FAIL — 'verdict ready-to-merge (), want boundary-violation'. artifactViolations came back EMPTY, so the backstop never fired.
- Same test alone, -run TestAForceAddedReportIsCaughtAtCollect: PASS.
- internal/exec/herdr alone, twice in a row: PASS, PASS (90s each).
- Full suite re-run: PASS.

So the guarantee itself is intact — it was verified passing on p6b's own commit f710ff5 and passes in isolation now. What is unreliable is the TEST under concurrency.

A flaky guarantee test is worse than a slow one: it can pass while the guarantee is broken, and it trains a reader to re-run rather than investigate. This one guards the artifact boundary, which two of four workers in wave 2 violated for real.

Where to look:
- The herdr harness gained SHARED state in wave 5: the fake herdr's workspaces map became map[string]harnessWorkspace and an agentGone flag was added (tick 5hz), and 'sort' came in with it. If harness instances share anything package-level, parallel tests interfere.
- 47t parallelised internal/reconcile and added a guard that every test either parallelises or says why. internal/exec/herdr was not its target, but the same question applies here and nothing enforces it.
- The failure mode is specifically that the BRANCH DIFF came back without the force-added path, which points at git work in a shared temp area or a worktree being read while another test writes it.

Run it under -race and with -count=N to reproduce before changing anything.
acceptance_criteria: The test passes 20 consecutive whole-suite runs, or the shared state that made it flaky is named and removed; go test -race on internal/exec/herdr is clean; the root cause is written down rather than the test being retried or skipped; if the herdr harness needs per-test isolation the way the reconcile fixtures have it, that isolation is added.
